problems: The lights on the shelf and along the bottom of the hut look like decorative string lights. Nothing in the picture says they mark places to grip, so a viewer who doesn't know the island won't link them to the caption's 'mark the two edges my claws could hold'.
The caption is about claws, but the bird's feet are cut off by the bottom edge of the frame. Its legs vanish below the picture, so the claws, the ledges and how they relate are never shown together.

The bird is also cut off on the right: its tail and back run out of the frame. It overlaps the front corner of the hut, so it's hard to tell whether it stands in front of the wall or is pushed into it.
The 'floor's rim' row of lights at the base is partly hidden behind the white flower clump and the bird's leg. Only a short stretch of that second edge can be seen.
The bird is just standing with its head turned toward the hut. Nothing in the picture shows it looking for something to climb or reaching toward either edge.
posts.critique: The picture is a pleasant shot of a bird next to a lit-up hut, but the caption's main claim, that the lights mark two edges its claws could hold, doesn't come across: the lights read as decoration and the claws are out of frame. The bird is cropped and pressed against the hut's corner, which makes the composition feel accidental.
